weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in the Genesis text itself (God gave every other tree freely, and the tree of life stood beside it) instead of a generic free-will argument, so the viewer learns something they did not already know.

Cut the familiar Exodus retelling and actually answer the why from Exodus 12 (the lamb dying in the household's place, 'when I see the blood, I will pass over you'), then end on a real question instead of a channel signpost.

weakest_line: People ask this in our comments all the time.
one_fix: Cut to the Cornelius story plus one other piece of evidence and drop the signposts and the denominational-disagreement paragraph; it is far too long and hedged for a Reel.
Open on the specific puzzle in the text (why would an all-knowing God ask Adam 'Where art thou?') instead of a sermon aimed at 'you', and stop assuming the viewer is hiding from God.

weakest_line: Work in that world would feel like tending something you love.
one_fix: Replace the speculation with what the text actually says about an unfallen world (the tree of life, Genesis 3:22) so the hook gets a concrete answer rather than imagined scenes.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Answer the 'forever' half of the hook, which the script raises and never addresses, and fix the muddled First/Second/Then/Third structure (Revelation 3 is also not 'how the Bible ends').
Cut the colleague-loses-job analogy entirely and let the Peter-versus-Judas contrast carry the takeaway; it is the strongest material and the analogy stalls the momentum right before it.

weakest_line: So the next time someone asks you where Cain's wife came from, you'll know what to say.
one_fix: Cut the restated hook and the 'most Christians can't answer it' line, and end on a genuine question that invites a response instead of 'you'll know what to say.'

weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Drop one of the three named thinkers (Schellenberg or Pascal) to cut the density for one listen, and end on the comment question without the channel tagline.

weakest_line: And when it worked, that never meant God approved.
one_fix: Make the ending question test the takeaway (can someone be powerfully used by God without God approving of how they live?) instead of the generic failures-or-prayer choice, and consider framing the hook around the more widely asked 'why did God keep using Samson?'
